newsitem.title: UK: LME tin hit by fund selling, slides to fresh low.
newsitem.headline: LME tin hit by fund selling, slides to fresh low.

text.p: LME tin slumped to the weakest level in over two years on Thursday afternoon as a bearish mood gripped the market after another stocks rise.
Most LME metals finished the day with losses, but copper and zinc rebounded from lows as speculative bulls showed confidence in uptrends which some analysts describe as overextended.
Three months tin dived to $5,580 per tonne, the lowest since March 1995, as fund liquidation and selling gained momentum in the wake of a 400-tonne stocks rise and shaky technicals.
Prices ended the day just off the lows at $5,600, a loss of $65.
"It is a lacklustre market with no bullish news whatsoever and with the stocks going up they just decided to sell it," said analyst Martin Squires of broker Rudolf Wolff.
Including Thursday's build, stocks have increased so far this week by 695 tonnes after a rise of 380 tonnes last week, bringing total inventories to 12,380 tonnes.
Squires said the target is now $5,500, with the next support at $5,420.
Copper held near its recent highs after a brief look at lower numbers on profit-taking sparked more speculative buying.
During the morning, a stock fall of 3,550 tonnes had emboldened prices to climb to $2,537, within a whisker of Wednesday's peak.
The charts indicate a correction is due, but fund and speculative buying keeps propping up the market.
"Yesterday's technical indicators did not confirm the new high so one has to watch out a bit," said Squires.
The 14-day RSI has remained in overbought territory above 70 since May 15.
The last time the RSI sustained a move above 70 was last November when it stayed there for 11 trading days. Thursday was the 10th successive trading day copper has held above the benchmark.
Zinc showed resilience after rebounding strongly from a slide to $1,341, to end with a loss of only $3 at $1,357.
It has been hovering at 4-3/4 year highs for the past several days but more tonnage showed up in the LME Singapore warehouse in Thursday's LME stocks data.

Traders had been hearing for weeks that Chinese zinc was on its way into Singapore but the actual increases were enough to shake confidence. Singapore inventories recorded 3,000 tonnes of inward deliveries on Wednesday and 4,300 tonnes on Thursday.
Despite the strong bounce, the market may be in for more tests of the downside, traders said.
Support was pegged at $1,332 and $1,324.
Aluminium got back into a downward groove, sliding to a $1,622 low, despite a 3,700-tonne stocks drawdown. It ended down $23 at $1,622.
The next important technical level is at $1,610, last Friday's low.
Nickel consolidated after its recent falls, ending unchanged at $7,280, while lead finished only $1 weaker at $640.
Alloy was indicated at $1,492/$1,497, down from $1,505/10.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
